sense: degree of an adjective or adverb

terms.comment: Quintilian’s word in grammar; in rhetoric the same word is hyperbole (Cic. de Or. 3.203).

evidence: Charis. p. 87; Prisc. p. 605 P. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The later grammarians’ gradus superlātīvus: doctissimus (Traupman 232). In the superlative is superlātīvē (Traupman 249): dīc «laetus» superlātīvē, give “laetus” in the superlative.

phrases.english: Give the superlative degree. — Most distant.

sources: Lewis & Short: superlatio · Lewis & Short: superlativus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 232, p. 244, p. 249.
